To understand "screen" as a verb, it helps to think about what physical screens actually do. A cinema screen displays images. A wire mesh screen on a window filters — it lets air in but keeps insects out. A decorative room divider conceals one part of a space from another. The verb "screen" borrows all three of these actions: to show, to filter, and to hide. Every meaning of the verb traces back to one of these three core ideas.
Meaning 1 — To show or broadcast a film or programme

When a film, documentary, or video is "screened," it is shown to an audience — in a cinema, on television, at a festival, or in any viewing setting.

"The director's debut film will be screened at the Cannes Film Festival."
"The documentary was screened on national television last night."

This meaning is straightforward: the film is put onto a screen for people to watch. "Screened" in this sense is interchangeable with "shown" or "broadcast," though it tends to sound slightly more formal and is often used in the context of events or public showings.
Meaning 2 — To examine, test, or check people or things in order to make a decision

This is the most widely used meaning in modern English, and it is the richest one. It comes from the image of a wire mesh sieve — the kind that lets certain particles fall through while holding back others. When you "screen" people or things, you are running them through some kind of test or evaluation to decide who or what passes and who or what does not.

This meaning appears across several important areas of life:

In medicine, to screen someone means to test them for a disease or health condition — usually before any symptoms have appeared — so that problems can be caught early and treated.

"All adults over 50 are encouraged to be screened for colon cancer."
"The clinic screened thousands of people for the virus during the outbreak."

The purpose of medical screening is early detection. It is a proactive test applied to a large group, not a diagnostic test for someone already feeling ill.

In employment, when a company screens applicants, it examines a large pool of candidates and filters them down to a smaller, more suitable group before moving to interviews or further stages.

"The HR department screened over 400 résumés before selecting 12 candidates for interviews."
"She was screened out early because she lacked the required qualifications."

Notice those two phrases — "screened in" and "screened out." To be screened in means you have passed the filter and moved forward in the process. To be screened out means you have been eliminated. These are very useful phrases to know.

In security, authorities screen people and their belongings at airports, courthouses, events, or any controlled area to check for weapons, prohibited items, or threats.

"All passengers must be screened before boarding the aircraft."
"Bags are screened using X-ray machines at the entrance."

For background checks, organisations screen individuals by looking into their past — criminal records, financial history, work references, and so on — before trusting them with a role or responsibility.

"The school screens all staff members before hiring."
"Volunteers who work with children are carefully screened."

In all of these contexts — medical, employment, security, background — the underlying logic is identical: a large, unfiltered group goes in, and a smaller, selected group comes out the other side. Some pass; some do not. That is the essence of this meaning.
Meaning 3 — To hide, shield, or protect something from view or harm

Here the verb draws on the idea of a physical room divider or a row of trees — something that acts as a barrier, blocking a view or protecting something behind it.

"A tall hedge screens the garden from the road." (The hedge hides the garden from people passing by.)
"She raised her hand to screen her eyes from the sun." (Her hand acted as a shield against the light.)
"A line of trees was planted to screen the factory from the surrounding neighbourhood."

In this sense, "screen" is close in meaning to shield, hide, block, or conceal. The key detail is that something — a physical object, a natural barrier, or even a person — is being placed between two things to prevent one from being seen or affected by the other.
Meaning 4 — To separate material by passing it through a mesh (technical)

In construction, engineering, mining, and geology, "to screen" means to pass raw material — gravel, sand, soil, ore — through a physical mesh screen so that particles of different sizes are separated. Smaller particles fall through; larger ones are held back.

"The workers screened the gravel to separate fine sand from larger stones."
"The ore was screened to remove large debris before processing."

This is the most literal and technical meaning, closest to the physical object. You are unlikely to encounter it in everyday conversation, but it is worth knowing.

This is a common everyday phrase that deserves its own explanation. To "screen" a phone call means to check who is calling before deciding whether to pick up — often by letting it ring or go to voicemail so you can assess it first.

"She never answers unknown numbers — she always screens her calls."
"His assistant screens all incoming calls before putting anyone through to him."

The logic here is again the filter: you are deciding which calls get through to you and which do not, rather than accepting every call blindly.

Whenever you see "screen" used as a verb, ask yourself which of these three actions is happening:

Showing → a film or programme is being displayed to an audience.
Filtering → people or things are being examined and sorted — some pass, some do not.
Hiding → something is being placed behind a barrier to block it from view or protect it from harm.

The filtering meaning is by far the most common in modern English. Whether it is a doctor testing patients, a company reviewing job applications, a security guard checking bags, or someone deciding not to pick up a phone call — in each case, there is a process of examination and selection at work, and the word for all of it is "screen."
